messages:
Maria: heads-up — multiple PROD customers reporting p99 spikes starting ~02:10 UTC after yesterday's runtime push. ticket ids 5543/5549. symptoms: very high GPU mem + occasional OOMs, but more often huge latency (p99 ~1.2s). attaching logs and quick repro below.

Maria: logs snippet from node gpu-12 (request id 3a2f9):
```
[02:12:03] runtime.INFO request=3a2f9 model=rw-13b ctx_len=8192 batch=1
[02:12:03] runtime.DEBUG gpu0.resident=15834MB gpu0.free=400MB cached_frag=24% kv_bytes=2.1GB
[02:12:03] runtime.ERROR cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (malloc_bytes=12,582,912)
[02:12:03] runtime.WARN falling back to host-buffering; token_generation_time=840ms
```

Maria: repro steps (minimal):
1) hit /v1/chat with model=rw-13b and a long convo (8k tokens)
2) followed by 3 concurrent prefix requests (small)
3) observe tail latency spike and sometimes a cudaMalloc error in node logs

Devon: ack. I'm pulling metrics now — looks like a cluster-wide p99 bump that lines up with the 02:05 deploy. dashboards show avg GPU resident jumps and a new pattern of long cudaMalloc stall times.

sre-bot: alert: p99_latency(cluster) crossed 900ms at 02:11 UTC; affected nodes: gpu-10,gpu-12,gpu-14; recent deploy id: rtd-20240327-rc3.

Lee: initial hypothesis: allocator fragmentation + growing KV cache per session. rc3 introduced per-request temporary buffers that were supposed to be pooled but I think pooling failed under long ctx loads. That will cause many small allocations, fragmentation, and then cudaMalloc falling back to slow path and host buffering.

Anita: can confirm KV growth pattern in traces — some customer sessions have KV size per-session > 2GB after long chats. We didn't GC inactive sessions aggressively; combined with fragmentation that will push us over.

Devon: quick triage checks I've run:
- top-of-host memory stable
- nvidia-smi shows high resident and a lot of reserved caching
- cudaMalloc time histogram: median ~0.2ms, 95th ~12ms, 99th ~420ms (bad)
- no increased gpu error rates aside from OOM fallback messages

Lee: immediate mitigation options (fast):
- enable runtime flag to cap per-request ctx to 4096 tokens for hosted tier (config flip)
- set runtime to drop or summarize oldest KV entries on sessions > 1GB (temporary LRU eviction)
- reduce concurrency on affected machines (scale down pods by 30%)

Lee: commands to flip cap via control plane API: 
```
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/runtime/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"max_context_tokens":4096}'
```

Simon: another fast win — flip on CUDA async allocator. On nodes with CUDA 11+ we can set env RW_ENABLE_CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC=1; should reduce fragmentation for many small allocs. I can patch the launch config and roll nodes in the next 15m.

Simon: note: cudaMallocAsync reduces latency for repeated small allocs but requires driver/kernel support; fallback path is safe. Will run canary on gpu-10 first.

Devon: rollback? It's an option but rollback will affect other fixes in rc3. I'd prefer try mitigations first (cap ctx + cudaMallocAsync + throttle) and monitor for 20-30m.

Maria: CS asked for ETA to restore p99 < 300ms. Can we give 'best effort' timeline? Customers are sensitive.

Anita: medium-term dev tasks:
- implement KV GC (evict stale entries after X inactivity, make it per-tenant) — owner: Anita — ETA: 2w
- fix pooling bug in rc3 path so buffers are actually reused across requests — owner: Lee — ETA: 5d
- add per-gpu fragmentation metrics (fragmentation ratio, cudaMalloc stalls) — owner: Devon — ETA: 3d

Lee: quick config PR arriving in 10m to enable max_context_tokens and an LRU kv eviction toggle. If CSR approves, we can flip it for hosted-tenants only.

Devon: running canary now with two changes: set max_context_tokens=4096 + RW_ENABLE_CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC=1 on gpu-10. I'll post results in 20m.

sre-bot: action created: incident/2024-03-27-memory-pressure assigned to @Lee @Devon @Anita, priority=P1.

Maria: thanks. I'll update the affected customers with this plan (cap + allocator change + throttling) and give a 1h initial ETA.

Lee: followups: after canary, if p99 drops, we will (1) roll change cluster-wide, (2) schedule a maintenance to rework allocator/pooling and deploy buffer-reuse patch, (3) implement a per-tenant max_kv_bytes guard.

Devon: canary update (02:31 UTC) — p99 on gpu-10 dropped from ~1.1s to ~250ms, cudaMalloc 99th dropped to ~18ms, kv bytes still high but eviction prevented growth. Canary looks good.

Maria: :thumbsup: please keep monitoring and post any regressions. I'll close customer loop when stable for 30m.

Simon: I'll start rolling RW_ENABLE_CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC to other nodes in batches of 2 and patch daemonset to include the env var.

Lee: created follow-up GH issues: #3148 (kv-gc), #3149 (allocator-pool-fix). Leaving this thread open until 30m stable window met.

Devon: metrics to capture going forward: per-gpu.resident_bytes, per-gpu.frag_pct, alloc_stall_histogram, per-session.kv_bytes. We'll add alerts at 90th frag_pct and sustained cudaMalloc 99th > 200ms.

Maria: closing note for records: root cause suspected = rc3 introduced broken buffer pooling + long chat KV growth -> fragmentation -> cudaMalloc stalls and OOM fallbacks -> p99 tail regression. mitigation = cap ctx, enable cudaMallocAsync, KV eviction, throttle concurrency; long-term = allocator rework + per-tenant KV guards.

Devon: thanks team. I'll post incident summary after 1h stable.
